advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that supplies a compatible_fingerprint predicate which raises and asserts the target/aggregate pin_status stays 'stale-pin-drift' (conservative fallback), exercising pin_health.py:172-180.
evidence:
pin_health.py:172-181: 'try:
                compatible = bool(
                    compatible_fingerprint
                    and compatible_fingerprint(...))
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - compatibility failure stays conservatively stale
                compatible = False
            status = "current" if compatible else "stale-pin-drift"'

The three tests in test_plan_material_pin_generation_3e0f.py all pass the real _legacy_material_ok predicate (via attest.derive_plan_material_pin_health) which does not raise for these inputs; none injects a compatible_fingerprint that raises, so the except branch (compatible=False) never executes.
The commit message and docstring explicitly introduce this as new behavior ('Keep ... compatibility failures conservatively stale'), yet it is not among the exercised cases.
advisory.finding: The newly introduced conservative-stale fallback in derive_health (the try/except wrapping compatible_fingerprint) is untested: no test forces compatible_fingerprint to raise, so the 'compatibility failure stays conservatively stale' contract has no regression guard and a change that let the exception propagate (crashing derive_health) would pass all tests.
scenarios: A future refactor removes or narrows the try/except and a raising compatibility predicate propagates, crashing derive_health for real pins instead of falling back to stale.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that calls pin_health.derive_health directly with a stub compatible_fingerprint that raises (e.g. lambda *_: (_ for _ in ()).throw(RuntimeError())) and a fingerprint returning a value != the pin, asserting pin_status == 'stale-pin-drift'.
